title: Handling Events
description: Learn how to handle user interactions like clicks, input changes, and form submissions.

data.text: **Events** are actions that happen in the browser - clicks, key presses, form submissions, etc. React events are similar to DOM events but with some syntactic differences.

data.title: Click Handler

data.text: Event handlers receive a **SyntheticEvent** object - React's cross-browser wrapper around the native event.

data.title: Using Event Object

data.text: Use `e.preventDefault()` to stop the browser's default behavior (like form submission reloading the page).

data.title: Prevent Default
Passing Arguments
data.text: To pass arguments to event handlers, use an arrow function: `onClick={() => handleClick(id)}`. Don't call the function directly: `onClick={handleClick(id)}` would execute immediately.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Pass function references, don't call them
Use e.preventDefault() to stop default behavior
Event handlers receive a SyntheticEvent object
data.takeaway: Events connect user actions to state updates. Let's learn best practices for managing state.
